name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: I’ll run a targeted benchmark on EXCAVA’s current excavator arm (serial #EXC-2024-07) using the latest CAT 349F L hydraulic pump (PN: 105-4457) to quantify baseline cycle time. I’ll log 50 full-dig cycles with the existing 1.2 m³ bucket (PN: 42-9101) in dry clay, then swap in the new 1.5 m³ HD bucket (PN: 42-9122) and repeat. The delta in average cycle time will be our 0.5%+ target metric.

name: Torque
text: Torque: Hold—your plan measures *cycle time*, but EXCAVA’s bottleneck isn’t bucket volume in dry clay—it’s the arm’s torque deficit under load. The CAT 349F’s pump PN: 105-4457 is a 2022 model; the 2024 spec (PN: 105-4468) adds 8% flow at 3,200 psi. Benchmark the *new* pump first—your baseline is already stale. Where’s the thermal stress test? Hydraulic oil temps spike 12°C with the HD bucket; cite the ISO 46 fluid spec you’ll use to prevent cavitation.

name: Gearbox
text:
Gearbox (power-w1): I’ll run a *torque-limited* benchmark on EXC-2024-07 with the new CAT 349F 2024 pump (PN: 105-4468) first—50 full-dig cycles in dry clay, logging arm torque at 3,200 psi via the onboard CAN bus (DBC: `excava_v3.dbc`, signals `ARM_TORQUE_REQ` and `PUMP_FLOW_ACT`). Then I’ll swap in the 1.5 m³ HD bucket (PN: 42-9102) and rerun the same test to isolate the torque bottleneck. Commands: `ros2 run excava_bench dig_cycle.py --pump 105-4468 --cycles 50 --log torque_data.csv` and `rostopic echo /arm/torque_feedback`.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-6351, worker-7892 — done, dissolved]

name: Torque
text: Torque: Hold—your torque-limited benchmark still assumes dry clay is the critical load case, but EXCAVA’s real-world bottleneck shifts to *mixed abrasive clay* (e.g., 30% moisture, 25% silica) where the arm’s linkage wear and hydraulic fluid viscosity dominate. Where’s the abrasion test data for the 2024 pump’s seals under 1,200-hour duty cycles? And why no thermal throttling check—those 3,200 psi spikes at 35°C ambient will shear the new pump’s compensator spring if the cooler’s bypass valve is undersized. Show me the *thermal envelope* before we waste cycles on a flawed baseline.

name: Dynamo
text:
DECISION: Run abrasion-weighted torque benchmarks on EXC-2024-07 with new 2024 CAT 349F pump (PN:105-4468) in mixed abrasive clay (30% moisture, 25% silica), logging `ARM_TORQUE_REQ`, `PUMP_FLOW_ACT`, and linkage wear via CAN bus (DBC: `excava_v3.dbc`).

Artifact must contain:
- 50-cycle torque/flow dataset in abrasive clay
- Wear metrics (linkage clearance, hydraulic viscosity delta)
- Comparative torque deficit vs. dry clay baseline
- 0.5%+ capability delta proof statement
